title: Drupal Patches Critical Core RCE Flaw with No-Login Path via Contributed Modules
summary: Drupal patched a critical security flaw in its software that could allow an attacker to run malicious code on a website's server. While the flaw cannot be reached by default, certain add-on modules create paths for attackers, including at least one that requires no login.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you run a website powered by Drupal, your web administrator or IT team needs to update the software immediately.
action_it: Apply the official updates released on October 14 (versions 11.4.10, 11.3.19, or 10.6.19) and review your Drupal installations for unauthorized access or suspicious activity related to contributed modules.

title: Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
summary: Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a security flaw in its firewall software that is currently being exploited in attacks. This vulnerability allows an attacker to run malicious code remotely.

also_covered.title: Palo Alto Networks Patches PAN-OS Authenticated RCE Flaw Amid Active Exploitation

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. This equipment is typically managed by company IT departments, not ordinary home users.
action_it: Apply Palo Alto Networks' security updates for PAN-OS immediately and check systems for signs of compromise.

title: Langflow's Critical Authenticated RCE Flaw Targeted in 1,423 Honeypot Exploit Attempts
summary: Hackers are actively attacking a critical security flaw in Langflow, a platform used to build artificial intelligence applications. This allows attackers to take control of vulnerable systems.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Langflow, your IT team should investigate and secure the system immediately.
action_it: Review systems running Langflow for signs of compromise and apply updates or mitigations provided by the vendor.

title: AhsayCBS Flaws Exploited to Deploy Web Shells Get New Fixes After Incomplete Patches
summary: Bad actors are exploiting flaws in AhsayCBS backup software to install malicious control tools and hidden cryptocurrency miners. Ahsay Backup has released new updates to fix these security holes after previous attempts fell short.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses AhsayCBS, your IT team should apply the security updates immediately.
action_it: Apply the latest security updates from Ahsay Backup for CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 to prevent unauthorized command execution, and check systems for signs of web shells or cryptocurrency miners.

title: Cisco Warns of Active Attacks Exploiting New Critical Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability
summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a critical security flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway devices using specially crafted emails. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to write files and run malicious commands with the highest level of system privileges.

also_covered.title: Cisco patches new Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Cisco Secure Email Gateway, your IT team needs to apply the updates provided by Cisco.
action_it: Apply the software patches provided by Cisco in their advisory to address the actively exploited zero-day flaw in Secure Email Gateway.

title: Fake AI Attacks Spread Across US Companies: How MSSPs Can Stop Incidents Early
summary: Attackers are tricking people with fake artificial intelligence products to spread malicious software and steal account data. This campaign is putting heavy pressure on companies that monitor cybersecurity for businesses.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything special beyond normal caution. Always double-check that you are downloading software from official, trusted websites rather than clicking random links or ads.
action_it: Security teams should monitor for unauthorized or suspicious AI tools being downloaded or used across the network. Educate employees on verifying the authenticity of software before installation.

title: GhostAction Compromises About 1,900 GitHub Accounts, Targets Over 30,000 Repositories
summary: A password-stealing campaign called GhostAction recently compromised nearly 1,900 GitHub accounts. It matters because the attackers targeted over 30,000 code repositories to steal sensitive secret keys.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you use GitHub, make sure you have turned on two-factor authentication (a security check requiring your phone or an app in addition to your password).

title: UK Legal Aid Agency: Hackers stole records dating back to 1978
summary: Hackers breached the IT systems of the UK Legal Aid Agency and stole records dating back to 1978. The attack exposes decades of sensitive legal aid information.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you are a client of the UK Legal Aid Agency, watch out for any suspicious communications using your personal details.
action_it: Investigate internal systems for signs of the April 2025 breach, review access logs, and follow standard incident response procedures for compromised government data.

title: Ledger asks sellers across Asia to halt sales after supply-chain attack
summary: Ledger has asked stores across several Asian countries to stop selling its crypto wallets while it investigates a supply-chain attack. This matters because physical tampering could allow attackers to steal cryptocurrency from the devices.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you bought a Ledger wallet from a reseller in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, or Hong Kong recently, contact Ledger support before using it.
action_it: Suspend sales and distribution of Ledger wallets across the affected Asian markets and await further guidance from Ledger regarding device verification and the investigation.

title: Microsoft fixes bug causing Windows black screens, Explorer crashes
summary: Microsoft fixed a bug that caused black screens and crashes on Windows 11. The issue is resolved, so no special action is needed.

title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2022 reached end of mainstream support
summary: Windows Server 2022 has reached the end of its mainstream support phase from Microsoft. It will continue to receive security updates under extended support until October 2031.

title: Police arrests 95 suspects in international CSAM crackdown action
summary: Police across 17 countries arrested 95 suspects in an international operation targeting online messaging groups that shared child abuse material. This action helps dismantle networks distributing illegal content.

title: Why AI Confidence Is Not Validation
summary: Artificial intelligence tools used in cybersecurity work are becoming more confident in their own outputs faster than humans can verify them. This creates a growing risk of unverified or incorrect information spreading outside of individual workstations.

title: India Mandates Registered Caller Name Display on 4G and Newer Networks From November 1
summary: The Indian government has ordered phone companies to display the registered names of callers on incoming calls starting November 1, 2026. This rule aims to help people spot spam and fraudulent calls from unknown numbers.

title: FBI raids DPRK IT worker laptop farms in Texas, US nationals arrested
summary: U.S. law enforcement seized nearly 187 laptops and arrested suspects involved in a North Korean remote IT worker scheme. This operation disrupted a foreign threat group's efforts to infiltrate U.S. companies using hidden identities.
